title: Pre-Analysis — Nose Wheel Steering Standard 3 Machined Manifold Retrofit
abstract: Pre-analysis of the retrofit case for the standard 3 machined steering manifold, covering the interim kit it replaces, the trouble shooting content that changes and the crew procedure that depends on residual steering authority.

sections.objective: Establish what a retrofit of the machined manifold involves on an aircraft already in service, as opposed to the production cut-in already achieved, and identify every published item that assumes the built-up manifold. The operators asking for the retrofit are the ones running the shortest sectors, so the pre-analysis was also asked whether the conversion could be built into a normal base visit rather than a standalone campaign.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and the retrofit was recommended with conditions. The interim filter kit is a genuine prerequisite in practice rather than on paper: an aircraft that never had it may still hold debris in the servo, and converting it without a servo flush moves the problem into a new manifold. The retrofit bulletin itself carries the pipe end fitting change and is the only place the seat angle difference is stated, which matters because a cross-fitted joint passes a static leak check and fails under pressure. The trouble shooting procedure changes at three steps because the filter cavity and the charging port move. The fourth finding is the flight crew procedure for a steering fault, which quotes a residual authority figure that is different after conversion; it was found by the similarity search rather than by any shared identifier and is exactly the kind of impact an engineer misses.
sections.next_steps: Write the retrofit to require either the interim kit or a servo flush as a pre-condition. Ask technical publications to restate the pipe end fitting seat angle in the removal task as well as in the bulletin. Raise the publication change requests for the trouble shooting procedure and for the flight crew entry together, so that the crew figure and the maintenance figure are issued at the same time.

similarity_seeds: machined manifold replacing a built-up assembly with integrated filtration
residual steering authority after a single channel failure

tasks.title: Establish whether the interim kit is a real prerequisite
Map the maintenance content that assumes the built-up manifold
Assess the flight crew procedure for a steering fault

expected_findings.rationale: An aircraft that never carried the interim kit may still hold debris in the servo. Converting it without a flush moves the problem straight into the new manifold.
expected_findings.resolution: Require either the interim kit or a servo flush as a pre-condition of the retrofit.

expected_findings.rationale: The bulletin carries the pipe end fitting change and is the only place the seat angle difference is stated. A cross-fitted joint passes a static leak check and fails under pressure.
expected_findings.resolution: Restate the seat angle in the removal task as well as in the bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The isolation procedure changes at three steps because the filter cavity and the accumulator charging port move onto the machined block face.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise a publication change request for the isolation procedure.

evidence.similarity_note: The crew entry describes holding the runway centreline and using differential braking; the modification text describes a machined manifold and pipe end fittings. They share no identifier and almost no vocabulary, yet the residual steering authority figure quoted to the crew changes after conversion.

expected_findings.rationale: The flight crew procedure quotes a residual authority after a single channel failure that is different on the converted aircraft. Nothing in the entity graph connects the two documents.
expected_findings.resolution: Issue the crew entry change at the same time as the maintenance content.

expected_non_findings.reason: Same chapter and the same nose and main gear vocabulary, but it introduces a coating on the main gear sliding tube and shares no part, no FIN and no zone with the steering manifold work.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position and two conditions. The retrofit is viable inside a normal base visit provided the servo history is addressed and the pipe end fitting standard is stated outside the bulletin.
